title: Customer Terms on Calling Off a Commission Before Delivery
content:
# Customer Terms on Calling Off a Commission Before Delivery

## Terms in force

A commission under Belrose Design Studio Custom Commissions cancelled before the design is approved is closed with nothing forfeited beyond any consultation deposit the programme takes.

The cancellation window is counted in whole calendar days from the day the design was approved, that day counting as day zero, weekends and studio holidays included. The date the customer approved the design is taken from the commission record, correlated by its commission reference, and the customer's recollection of that date does not stand in for it.

A piece already finished is not refunded at all, because it was made to that customer's own specification and cannot be sold on.

The cancellation is confirmed by the customer on the commission service request record, because walking away from a piece being made for them is theirs alone to do.

## Counting the window (hypothetical)

Under a programme whose cancellation window is 7 calendar days, with the design approved on the 10th of a month: the 17th is day 7 and the last day within the window, and the 18th is day 8 and outside it. Weekends and studio holidays falling in between are counted like any other day.

## Terms no longer in force

Four sentences of the earlier wording of these terms have been superseded by the current basis and are **no longer in force**. They are recorded so that they are not applied:

> "A commission is cancelled without the heavier forfeit only when the request reaches the studio within the cancellation window in calendar days, counted from the date the customer approved the design." — no longer in force.

> "Cancelled before production begins, the commission forfeits the programme's lighter share of the quoted total; cancelled once production has begun, it forfeits the programme's heavier share" — no longer in force.

> "the deposit's non-refundable share is never returned in either case" — no longer in force.

> "The refund is what the customer has paid to date less what is forfeited, and where the forfeit exceeds what was paid nothing further is collected from the customer." — no longer in force. Under that retired clause nothing further was collected from the customer where what was forfeited came to more than what had been paid.
